Final-composite/tonemap of the globe SURFACE body (not a fullscreen post pass). Reads many work RTs and writes ocol0 to a 512-wide target. The *8 then LUT(tex15/tex14) is HDR exposure then tonemap-curve via two Y16_X16_FLOAT LUTs; tex14/tex15 are 2-channel float LUTs (only .xy of tex15 and .zw of tex14 are used, packing 4 output channels). tex13 (display/feedback RT) is added at 0.125 weight to BOTH halves -> a uniform feedback/dither term added post-tonemap.

It READS tex13 = current display/feedback RT and ADDS onto it (feedback term), so run it AFTER whatever wrote tex13. It WRITES to a 512-class target (earth-surface/work layer), not directly the 1920x1080 present.

(4) sampler coord xforms (texture_parameters scale/bias/clamp) are identity-ish here in the dump; if a tex needs flip/clamp apply COORD_SCALE per TEX_PARAM. (5) const2/6/7 are identical, const14/18 share x with const4 - all inlined per their used swizzle. (6) ROP does round_to_8bit on output in HW; only matters for exact bit-match.

NOTE the y axis is internally compressed by const1.z=0.2 inside the FP (tc0.y*0.2), and the per-axis tap offsets come from the tex1 LUT (const3/const4 = 0.025 magnitude), NOT from the VP. There is no VP-supplied texel-step constant; the resample step/offsets are entirely LUT- and FP-const-driven.
notes: Output RT: writes col0=r0 (RGBA) with blending disabled, so it overwrites its bound color target (this small full-screen quad is a resample/soft-bloom step over the 40x40 tex0 into the work layer). It READS tex0 (40x40, 0x07b06400) as the source layer and tex1 (128x1, 0x07af8800) as a fractional-interpolation coefficient table. The 9 other bound textures (tex2..tex15) are NOT referenced by the microcode (FP only declares uniform sampler2D tex0/tex1) and must be omitted from the port. CAVEATS: (1) tex1 sampler needs scale_x=1/128 (its width) to convert the pixel-space index (tc0*40-0.5) to UV; I inlined that as *(1/128) in TEX1. tex0 taps are already 0..1 UV (tc0 +/- 0.025*LUToffset) and use straight bilinear. (2) const1.z=0.2 means the y coordinate only spans a 0.2-tall band of tc0 before the *40 grid scale, so the kernel footprint is anisotropic (wider in y texel-space). (3) The kernel is a separable 2x2 weighted blend: per-axis the LUT gives 2 weights (r2.z/r2.w for x, r3.z/r3.w for y) and 2 signed sub-texel offsets (r2.x/r2.y, r3.x/r3.y) -> classic firmware bicubic/Catmull-Rom-via-LUT upsample. (4) Final line is a contrast/overshoot: r0 = h0*(1 + clamp(h0*4/3,0,1)*(1/3)), brightening highlights up to ~1.33x while leaving blacks unchanged. (5) primitive=8 is a quad/triangle-strip of 4 verts (full-screen).

CHAINING / SEMANTICS:
- This is a per-vertex textured glow MESH pass (primitive=6 triangle strip, 3232 verts for draw 17, 400 for draw 18), NOT a screen quad and NOT a separable blur. There is no texel-step constant. The only color source is tex0 = the 256x128 glow accumulation layer at RT 0x06e80000; it is sampled ONCE at UV (vUV.x, 5.0*vUV.y) (vertical 5x stretch via 1/c1.z).
- The fp computes two smoothstep falloff factors from UV.y (t1 = smoothstep over 25*vUV.y; t2 = smoothstep over a band coordinate (5*vUV.y - 0.608)/0.392) but with THESE draw constants the alpha/exp path collapses: r2.x = r3.w*r1.w - r3.y = 1 - 1 = 0, so the exp2(-10.4*vUV.x) horizon-falloff term is multiplied by 0 and never contributes, r0.w (alpha) stays 0, and L681/L682 reduce to color = tex0.rgb * 0.508002 * 8.0 * (1 - r1.y). Net RGB before LUT = tex0.rgb * 4.064016 * (1 - smoothstep(t2)).
- Final RGB is NOT the raw computed color: it is passed through the float tonemap LUTs. R,G come from tex15 indexed by (computed r0.x, r0.y); B comes from tex14 indexed by (clamp16(r0.z), max(r0.x,r0.y)). tex15=0x02b70000, tex14=0x02b90000, both 128x128 Y16_X16_FLOAT (2 valid channels). For the port these LUTs must be supplied as the real float textures dumped from RPCS3 (Y16_X16_FLOAT) - approximating them defeats the tonemap. Both LUTs are read in CLAMP-to-edge with linear filtering as per the RT sampler params.
- ALPHA output is exactly 0.0 for every fragment under these constants. Blend ENABLE=0 so output is written directly (the src=773/dst=772 ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA/SRC_ALPHA factors in the record are inactive). If this pass is later composited, note the written alpha is 0.
- precision_clamp here is just clamp with NaN->0; clamp16 = clamp(x,-65504,65504). fma(a,b,c)=a*b+c preserved. rcp(x)=1/x, div(a,b)=a/b preserved. The r1.x in L660 still holds vUV.x (=tc0.x*1) at that point, so r1.x = -vUV.x*10.4. tc0.z and tc0.w from the vertex shader are never read by the fp.

notes: Trivial single-tap pass: out = texture(bloomLevel, uv) * 9.24721, blended ADDITIVELY (src=1 dst=1) into the destination RT. This is a bloom upsample/accumulate step: one pyramid level (256x128 @ 0x027a0000) is read, scaled by the per-draw gain const[0].x, and added on top of whatever is already in the bound color target. The gain value (here 9.24721) is per-draw and changes between consecutive accumulate draws (cf. draw 54 uses 25.2329 with the same vp and same shape but a different fp/source level), so the gain must be sourced from the draw's const[0].x at runtime, not hard-coded, when chaining multiple accumulate passes. fs_main samples ONLY tex0/tc0; the other bound textures (tex1 display, tex2/tex3 512x512, tex4 256x128, tex5 256x1 ramp, tex6 64x64, tex13 dither, tex14/tex15 tonemap LUTs) are bound by the pipeline but NEVER read by this fragment program. All channels rgba are written (the multiply replicates const0.x across all 4). Helpers: TEX2D(0,uv)=texture(tex0,uv) (no COORD scale/bias on this pass); _fetch_constant(0).xxxx = vec4(9.24721). No clamp16/fma/rcp used in this shader. Output register is r0 (#define col0 r0).

notes: Fullscreen-quad bloom/glow accumulate pass. Reads ONLY tex0 = the 512x256 glow/blur layer B at RT 0x02660000 (despite 10 textures being bound; tex1-tex15 are leftover bindings the fp never samples). Multiplies the entire RGBA texel by the scalar gain const[0].x = 25.2329 (broadcast via .xxxx to all 4 channels, including alpha) and writes it with ADDITIVE blending (blend=1, src=1, dst=1) into whatever destination RT this draw targets, accumulating a bright bloom contribution. No coordinate transforms, no blur taps, no LUTs, no tonemap, no clamp16 in the math. To chain: this is one of the additive bloom-pyramid upsample/accumulate steps; the destination RT (not given in dc.txt line, infer from pass graph) receives glow-layer-B * 25.2329 added on top. The large gain (~25x) compensates for the small/quantized HDR values stored in the low-res glow layer. Note DRAW 55 immediately after uses the SAME vp and an analogous fp (9efe1b93...) but samples tex0=0x02360000 (the main HDR work/glow layer) instead, i.e. a sibling accumulate of a different source layer with the same additive blend.

notes: Single-draw post step (draw 56). Reads tex1 = glow/blur ping-pong layer at 0x02560000 (512x256) and the 32x32 dither texture (tex13, 0x0791f980). Writes its result with ADDITIVE blend (ONE/ONE) onto its destination RT. Math is exactly: ocol0.rgb = tex1.rgb*1.0 - dither.rgb*0.125 ; ocol0.a = 0.0 - dither.a*0.125. notes: PASS GRAPH ROLE: This is the stars/nebula HDR encode pass. It samples the DXT1 stars texture (tex0 @0x07952c00) over the full screen and re-encodes it through the two FLOAT tonemap LUTs (tex15 @0x02b70000 and tex14 @0x02b90000, both Y16_X16_FLOAT 2-channel) into an LDR color, then ADDITIVELY blends (src=1 dst=1) the result into the destination RT (the HDR work/composite layer). tc0.xy is a plain screen-space UV from the fullscreen quad vp. CHAINING: needs the stars texture decoded + the two 2-channel float LUTs uploaded; output is added on top of whatever is already in the bound color target. CAVEATS: (1) The two LUTs are 2-channel FLOAT (Y16_X16) so in WebGL you need RG float textures or a 2-ch decode; only .x/.y of LUT15 and .z(=as authored) of LUT14 are read. (2) The LUT lookup coordinates are extremely small numbers (~9.7e-6 * exp2(...)*8), i.e. nearly 0 in UV; the actual mapping shape lives entirely in the LUT data, so a faithful port REQUIRES the real LUT texels, not a formula. (3) Output A = r1.y = exp2(G*8.64386) * 9.7e-6 (no LUT). (4) clamp16 not used in this shader; no precision_clamp needed. (5) const2.x / const5.x (0.000194) and const2.y (2.1493) recur but only the lanes noted are read. Exact final: ocol0 = vec4(LUT15(uv).x, LUT15(uv).y, LUT14(uv2).z, r1.y).

notes: FINAL COMPOSITE/COPY pass. Reads main HDR work layer (tex0 @ 0x02360000) and writes additively into the display/present RT (0x0dc80000). It is effectively a 1:1 copy of the HDR scene plus a dither term: ocol0.rgb = tex0.rgb + dither.rgb*0.125; ocol0.a = 1.0 + dither.a*0.125. Because blend is ADDITIVE (ONE/ONE), this layer ACCUMULATES the work layer onto whatever is already in the display (e.g. stars/background drawn earlier). The dither tex13 (32x32, fmt 0xe5) is sampled in screen space (window pos / 32, wrap repeat) to break banding in the HDR->8bit present; weight 0.125 (=1/8 of a unit, i.e. ~32 in 0..255 scaled by the dither's small values). The 0xe5 format is a low-magnitude noise pattern; chain it as a tiled 32x32 ordered/blue-noise texture. CAVEAT: vc[4] (vp screen-quad/flip constants) and the tex0/tex13 sampler scale/bias were not in the const dump; identity UV + 1/32 dither tiling assumed from RT sizes and the fullscreen-quad role. ROP rounding (round_to_8bit) and additive ONE/ONE blend happen after fs_main. No alpha test effect (func from rop_control, alpha_ref not dumped; alpha=~1.0 passes typical >=/always). Many bound samplers (tex1..tex6,tex14,tex15) are NOT referenced by this fp - they are leftover bindings from prior bloom/tonemap passes.

role: stars/point-sprite HDR glow billboard: analytic anisotropic radial falloff (exp), gated by a reflection-vector length test, tone-mapped through two FLOAT LUTs (tex15 = RG out, tex14 = B out). Additive blend over the HDR work layer.
output_channels: rgb (r0.xyz written from LUTs; r0.w left as gated-falloff value from r0=r1*h0.x). Meaningful color = rgb. Alpha = gated falloff (used by SRC_ALPHA blend factor 770).
blend: additive-ish: blend=1 src=770 (GL_SRC_ALPHA) dst=1 (GL_ONE). result = src.rgb*src.a + dst.rgb. Note src.a = r0.w = gated radial falloff.
vp_texcoords: NOT a blur. Per-vertex point-sprite/billboard. vp 48ad6e9761419744: in_pos=read_location(0). tc0=dst_reg7=(in_pos.xy + const7.x)*const7.y ; with this draw's vc const7=(1,1,1,1) => tc0.xy = in_pos.xy + 1.0 (sprite-local coord; fp then subtracts 0.5 via fp-const0). tc1=dst_reg8 = r0_view.xyz - const8.xyz, where r0_view = (dot(pos,vc0),dot(pos,vc1),dot(pos,vc2)) i.e. a 3x4 view-matrix transform of the vertex; tc1 is the view-space ray/direction. fp multiplies tc1 by gl_FragCoord.w (perspective-correct interpolation undo) before normalizing. gl_Position uses vc3..vc6 (clip-space rows). No texel-step constant (this is geometry, not a screen-quad blur).
notes:
WHAT IT IS: per-point HDR glow/star sprite, NOT a screen-space blur. Reads ONLY the two 128x128 FLOAT tonemap LUTs (tex15=0x02b70000, tex14=0x02b90000). The other 8 bound textures (tex0..tex6,tex13) are bound by RSX state but NEVER sampled by this fp -- ignore them for the port. 

MATH SUMMARY: 
 - sprite-local coord uv = tc0.xy - 0.5 in [-0.5,0.5].
 - anisotropic L1 radial term D = abs(uv.x)*9.40005 + abs(uv.y)*10.1 ; falloff = exp2(-D*1.4427) = exp(-D)  (Gaussian-like elliptical, slightly taller than wide).
 - V = normalize(tc1*gl_FragCoord.w) (view ray). reflect-ish vec R = V*dot(V,-A)+A with A=(1.4291,1.77865,-0.315622). gate = (length(R) >= 1.0)?1:0. (A is a fixed light/anti-light direction; the gate is a hemisphere/backface-style cull so only points on one side glow.)
 - g = falloff * gate (scalar, replicated to all of r0).
 - OUTPUT: rgb from LUTs at coord (g*8, g*8): r0.rg = tex15(vec2(g*8)).rg ; r0.b = tex14(vec2(g*8)).b(=.z, but 2ch LUT so likely .y mapped; KEEP .z swizzle verbatim). r0.a = g (drives SRC_ALPHA blend). 
 - LUT coords (g*8,g*8) with g in [0,1] exceed [0,1] range -> rely on LUT sampler clamp/wrap (CLAMP per texture_parameters). The LUTs convert the linear falloff*8 into the final HDR star color/brightness (tonemap curve). 

CHAINING: writes to whatever RT is bound as color0 for these draws (additive HDR accumulation, src_alpha/one). It accumulates star/point glows onto the HDR layer. Inputs (LUTs) are produced by an earlier tonemap-LUT-bake pass. gl_FragCoord.w must be exposed (1/w) for the perspective-correct ray normalization; in a fullscreen WebGL reimplementation of a single point this is supplied by the rasterizer when drawing actual point geometry, NOT a fullscreen quad. To port faithfully you must draw the same point primitives (primitive=8, 4 verts each = quads/billboards), feeding per-vertex in_pos and the view matrix (vc0..2) + clip matrix (vc3..6) + const7/const8 from the vp constants.

CAVEAT/FLAGGED: the exact LUT contents (tex14/tex15 FLOAT 128x128) must be dumped and used as-is (2-channel Y16_X16_FLOAT); do not approximate the tonemap curve. The .z fetch from a 2-channel LUT (tex14) is kept verbatim from the microcode; verify channel mapping against the dumped LUT when wiring up.

role: multi-tap mip-blur textured screen quad with per-vertex tint (degenerates to plain textured quad at this draw's constants: level const[0]=0 < threshold 0.2, so both blur branches are skipped -> output = tex0(tc0.xy) * saturate(diff_color))
blend: additive-ish alpha blend: blend=1 src=770(GL_SRC_ALPHA) dst=771(GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) -> standard src-over alpha blend (out = src.rgb*src.a + dst.rgb*(1-src.a))
vp_texcoords: VP is NOT a blur tap generator. tc0 (=dst_reg7) is produced as tc0.xy = in_normal.xy * vc[4].xy + vc[4].zw (the ATTR2 "normal" stream is repurposed as the source UV; vc[4] is a UV scale.zw / bias). tc0.zw left at default (0,1). diff_color (the per-vertex tint, location=1) = in_weight(ATTR1) * vc[5]. gl_Position = dot(in_pos, vc[0..3]) i.e. a plain 4x4 transform of a 4-vertex quad. So in the FP, tc0.xy is just the screen/quad UV and diff_color is a uniform-per-draw tint multiplier. There are NO per-vertex tap offsets; all the multi-tap sampling in the FP is computed in-shader from fragment constants (a manual box/bilinear mip-blur), gated by const[0] vs const[1]. The texel step for those internal taps comes from fc[3].y, fc[4].x, fc[6].y, fc[7].x (all 4 / 0.5 here) NOT from the VP.
